correctness.rationale: For G=K_m,n-M_t, PIDF labels {0,1,2} and requires open-neighborhood weight exactly two at each zero. Shore sums X,Y imply a matched zero a_i sees Y-y_i; unmatched zero sees Y, and analogously other shore. A total weight <=3 forces one entire shore positive; checking sizes 2 and 3 yields precisely m=2,t=0 weight2, m=2,t=1 or (2,3,2),(3,3,3) weight3; otherwise a deleted matched positive pair labeled2+2 (or t=0 one label2 per shore) realizes weight4. At weight4 with zeros on both shores, X=Y=2 and every deleted matched pair has synchronized positive support, so summing the support sizes a,b=1,2 over s shared deleted indices yields C(m,n,t). The only extra all-positive-shore exceptions are (3,3,2) twice and (3,4,3) once; (2,2,2) has 9 via two isolated K_2 components. Independent direct exact-neighborhood enumeration verified both optimum and count for all 2<=m<=4,m<=n<=5,0<=t<=m. Finite tests do not prove unrestricted classification.
